clue.text: Sweet drink taken by a goat, say.

indicators.note: the drink is taken on by the goat, so it follows the goat's word

parts.note: a goat butts, so it can be called a butter, one that butts
Scotch is whisky, a drink

explanation.surface: A goat is offered a sweet drink and laps it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The goat is not an animal here but a 'butter', something that butts; 'say' flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard toffee-like confection, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Enthusiast taking a look at cattle

parts.note: a buff is a keen fan, as in film buff
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A fan of livestock goes to inspect the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo are large wild oxen, kinds of cattle.

clue.text: Ship duty appears to upset, say, a couple of Poles

indicators.note: the pool of letters is knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means
N is north pole; two of them give NN

explanation.surface: A tax on shipping appears to upset two Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is kept as written and 'upset' shuffles the rest. 'Poles' are not people from Poland but the magnetic poles, written N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage was historically a tax levied per ton of a vessel's cargo capacity.

clue.text: He may put on a semi-transparent coat

definitions.text: He may put on a semi-transparent coat

parts.words: He may put on a semi-transparent coat
parts.note: the coat is not clothing but a glassy layer fired onto metal or pottery, applied by a craftsman

explanation.surface: A man dons a see-through jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: This craftsman applies vitreous glaze to metal or ceramics, a glossy translucent layer.

clue.text: Comes to a half in a grassy area

annotationWithheld.why: Comes to a half (scan: halt) in a grassy area: grassy area = SWARD, with 'Comes to a halt' as DRAWS UP, i.e. DRAWS read up the down light; no clue word but the definition phrase signals the reversal, so it does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Comes to a half in a grassy area

clue.text: Supply with excessive weaponry, making deliveries thus?

definitions.meaning: to give too many weapons, to arm beyond need
in cricket a bowler delivers the ball with the arm swung above the shoulder

explanation.surface: Over-arming a force is compared with the way a bowler delivers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each ball bowled is a 'delivery'; the second definition is a description of bowling style.
explanation.definitionFit: The word reads as over-arm, to equip with too many weapons, and as a cricket style of bowling with the hand high.

clue.text: Vessel suitable for the Owl's companion?

definitions.text: Vessel suitable for the Owl's companion?

parts.words: Vessel suitable for the Owl's companion?
parts.note: in Edward Lear's poem the Owl sails with the Pussy-cat, so a boat for the feline companion

explanation.surface: A nonsense-verse boat is chosen for a bird's sailing partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear's 'The Owl and the Pussy-cat' went to sea in a beautiful pea-green boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catboat is a small sailing boat with one mast set far forward, a real kind of vessel.

clue.text: This may draw attention to cases involving a charge.

definitions.text: This may draw attention to cases involving a charge.

parts.words: This may draw attention to cases involving a charge.
parts.note: the cases are not legal ones but buried explosive casings, which an instrument signals

explanation.surface: A lawyer's tool highlights criminal cases with an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: This device finds buried explosives, whose casings hold a charge.

clue.text: King of Spain's daughter's admirer in modern army

parts.note: taken as written
a fan is an admirer
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force formed in the twentieth century

explanation.surface: A Spanish princess has a devotee serving in today's army.
explanation.walkthrough: The admirer is read as being 'in modern army', a phrase that splits around it. 'The King of Spain's daughter' comes from the nursery rhyme 'I Had a Little Nut Tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese monarch, a royal princess.

clue.text: One who helped when Miss Davis fell into a river?

indicators.note: the actress's name drops inside the letters made by the following words

parts.note: Bette Davis was the Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A rescuer is described: someone who helped when an actress tumbled into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Abetter is a legitimate spelling of abettor, one who aids.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, so an abetter is an accomplice or helper.

clue.text: Ordinary freedom: Tomand Maggie Tulliver enjoyed when young?:

definitions.text: freedom: Tomand Maggie Tulliver enjoyed when young?:
definitions.meaning: George Eliot's siblings grew up at Dorlcote Mill, so the liberty to roam it

explanation.surface: Two literary children enjoy an everyday kind of liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom and Maggie Tulliver are the brother and sister of George Eliot's 'The Mill on the Floss'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unremarkable, and literally the freedom to wander about a mill.

clue.text: Athenian character with reputation backs issue

indicators.note: backs here means goes into reverse, so the combined run of letters is read from the end

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character an Athenian would write
your name is your reputation, as in making a name

explanation.surface: Someone from Athens with a good reputation supports an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces in clue order, and 'backs' turns the whole run backwards; 'backs' looks like support but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or proceed from a source, the verb sense of issue.

clue.text: Keep going to imprison old soldier

indicators.note: the letters for 'old' are locked up inside the phrase for keeping going

parts.note: to drag on is to keep going tediously

explanation.surface: An elderly soldier is told to continue his duty of jailing prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' looks like part of 'old soldier' but supplies only its O; the definition is 'soldier'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, a type of cavalry soldier.

clue.text: Wear down the king with literary work.

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward
an ode is a lyric poem, a literary work

explanation.surface: A monarch is worn down by the burden of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water does rock.

clue.text: Airy-sounding moment-apt to return in Wagnerian opera?

indicators.note: the word for airy is heard, not spelt, giving a German-looking spelling

parts.note: airy means light, as in not heavy
MO is a moment, as in 'half a mo'

indicators.note: the word for apt comes back, so its letters run in reverse

parts.note: fit means apt or suitable

explanation.surface: A breezy moment comes round again in an opera by Wagner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns LIGHT into LEIT; 'to return' turns FIT into TIF.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner built his operas on recurring musical themes tied to characters and ideas.

clue.text: In disguise, removing in case of recognition, perhaps?

definitions.text: removing in case of recognition, perhaps?
definitions.meaning: travelling about under a false name so as not to be known

explanation.surface: Someone disguises themselves and moves on for fear of being recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' here means moving away, as one might travel under an assumed identity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes having one's identity concealed, and travelling so as to avoid being known.

clue.text: Odd contrivance for changing motion

definitions.meaning: in engineering, a disc mounted off-centre on a shaft that turns rotation into back-and-forth movement

explanation.surface: A strange gadget is described as altering the way things move.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who is unconventional and an off-centre mechanical disc driving reciprocating motion.

clue.text: Nurse is in church 'without her

indicators.note: the verb and pronoun together go inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: her, taken as written; 'without' in its old sense of outside places the pronoun on the outer side of the little verb
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse is at church, but her absence is noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense means outside, so the pronoun stands before the verb inside the church abbreviation; the surface reading of 'without' as lacking is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a hope or feeling is to hold it dear and foster it.

clue.text: Sounds like Paul Revere's compound!

indicators.note: the description of his ride is heard and spelt as the chemical word

parts.note: Paul Revere's famous midnight gallop in 1775 is a ride at night

explanation.surface: An American patriot's ride is compared to a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere rode at night to warn of advancing British troops in the American Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a chemical compound of nitrogen with another element.

clue.text: Not a friendly type this columnist

definitions.text: Not a friendly type this columnist

parts.words: Not a friendly type this columnist
parts.note: the clue's columnist is not a newspaper writer but a traitor working from within, named by its ordinal word

explanation.surface: An unpleasant newspaper columnist is described.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'fifth columnist' is a secret sympathiser of the enemy; the answer is the word that goes with 'columnist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifth column is the phrase for internal traitors, so this is the ordinal that precedes columnist.

clue.text: Acting unwisely like Trinculo

definitions.meaning: Trinculo is the jester in Shakespeare's The Tempest, acting as a clown

explanation.surface: Someone behaves unwisely like a Shakespearean jester.
explanation.definitionFit: The participle means messing about stupidly, and also playing the jester as Trinculo does.

clue.text: Smith's father embracing Emma's protégé endlessly

definitions.note: read as 'Smith is', the 's acting as a verb

indicators.note: the priest's abbreviation holds the trimmed name inside it

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: the name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Harriet Smith is the young woman Emma takes under her wing in Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: Smith's father hugs the girl Emma took up, in Austen's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' takes the first and last letters off the protégé's name, and 'embracing' wraps the priest's abbreviation round what is left. 'Smith' looks like Harriet's surname but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrier shoes horses, a kind of blacksmith.

clue.text: The new rate for the writing and production of plays.

definitions.text: the writing and production of plays

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a new version of the word rate reshuffles its letters

explanation.surface: A new charge is set for writing and staging plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like a link word but is kept as it stands; only 'rate' is shuffled, signalled by 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre as an art is the work of writing and staging drama.

clue.text: Partially revise a Glenn Miller score

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to revise part of a Glenn Miller arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glenn Miller' suggests the bandleader's music; the definition is a golf score, as by golfer Johnny Miller.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf two under par on a hole is called by this bird's name.

clue.text: Almost a giant wearing lightweight fabric

indicators.note: the gram goes round the cut-down giant like clothing

parts.note: a gram is a tiny unit of weight

indicators.note: the giant loses its final letter, being nearly complete

parts.note: an ogre is a giant of fairy tales

explanation.surface: A near-giant is dressed in a light cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the giant's last letter and 'wearing' puts what is left inside the weight. 'lightweight fabric' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'fabric' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Grogram is a coarse cloth of silk mixed with mohair or wool.

clue.text: Monarch sick and complaining bitterly

parts.note: R stands for Rex or Regina, a monarch
ailing means sick

explanation.surface: An ill monarch grumbles bitterly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest angrily, so this is the participle of scolding vehemently.

clue.text: Sign briefly in the first place

definitions.meaning: to sign with just the first letters of one's name
at the beginning, as in the opening stage

explanation.surface: A signature is dashed off at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to mark with abbreviated name letters; as an adjective it means at the outset.

clue.text: Perhaps one emerges with honour as a trader in Leicester

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award

indicators.note: the following words are offered as a possible jumble, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is decorated and becomes a merchant in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges the two words 'one emerges', and 'with' sets the award's letters beside them. Leicester is not the city but Red Leicester, an English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of cheese deals in varieties such as Red Leicester.
